meaning:
βεβαίωσις, -εως, ἡ
(βεβαιόω, which see), [in LXX: Lev.25:23 (צְמִיתֻת), Wis.6:19 * ;]
confirmation: τ. εὐαγγελίου, Php.1:7; εἰς β., Heb.6:16, a phrase frequently in π. of guarantee in a business transaction (Deiss., BS, 104ff.; Cremer, 140).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: It is even right for me to think this way on behalf of all of you, because I have you in my heart, because both in my bonds and in the defense and confirmation…
For men indeed swear by a greater one, and in every dispute of theirs the oath is final for confirmation.
